texts.preamble: Anil Kumar vs State Of U.P. on 21 January, 2021 Author: Siddharth Bench: Siddharth High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad ?Court No. - 73 Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 27 of 2021 Applicant :- Anil Kumar
texts.facts: Govind Mishra @ Chhotu Versus State of U.P., hence, this anticipatory bail application is being Anil Kumar vs State Of U.P. on 21 January, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134071052/ 1 heard. Grant of further time to the learned A.G.A as per Section 438 (3) Cr.P.C. (U.P. Amendment) is not required. There is allegation in the F.I.R. regarding recovery of illegal liquor from applicant. It has been submitted that offence under Section 60 (1) of Excise Act is bailable and triable by Magistrate but offence u/s 272 I.P.C. is non-bailable. But under Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, complaint was required to be filed. False recovery has been alleged against the applicant. The applicant has definite apprehension that he may be arrested by the police any time.
texts.arguments: Learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail of the applicant. He has submitted that in view of the seriousness of the allegations made against the applicant, he is not entitled to grant of anticipatory bail. The apprehension of the applicant is not founded on any material on record. Only on the basis of imaginary fear, anticipatory bail cannot be granted. In the case of Joginder Kumar v. State of Uttar Pradesh AIR 1994 SC 1349, the Apex Court has referred to the third report of National Police Commission wherein it is mentioned that arrests by the police in India is one of the chief source of corruption in the police. The report suggested that, by and large, nearly 60 percent of the arrests were either unnecessary or unjustified and that such unjustified police action accounted for 43.2 percent of expenditure of the jails. Personal liberty is a very precious fundamental rights and it should be curtailed only when it becomes imperative. According to the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case, the arrest of an accused should be made. Without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case and considering the nature of accusation and his antecedents, the applicant is entitled to be released on anticipatory bail for limited period in this case considering the exceptions considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sushila Aggarwal vs. State (NCT of Delhi)- 2020 SCC Online SC 98.
